editors-message.title: Clear Skies ahead
editors-message.byline: Caitlin Bernal and Gabriel Renee Quizan
editors-message.article:
SOARING ABOVE lofty expectations, the Ateneo Blue Eagles showcased a series of outstanding and historic performances in the first semester of the University Athletic Association of the Philippines’ (UAAP) Season 88. Across a nine-sport schedule, the Blue and White brought home eight podium finishes and three championships—a testament to the exemplary caliber embodied forth by the University’s student-athletes.

With the UAAP gearing up for a packed second-semester slate, the Blue Eagles look to end Season 88 on a high note as they carry the Ateneo banner with beaming pride and fiery resolve.

The second installment of Season 88 will follow 20 teams on 20 different journeys, all united by a single goal of reaching the UAAP pinnacle. This semester’s primer aims to reemphasize the collective drive and passion embodied by the Blue Eagles.

As the dedication to attaining greatness intensifies in Loyola Heights, The GUIDON Sports remains an attentive chronicler of the unique Atenean sportsperson journey. From the Blue Eagles’ pursuit of knowledge in the classroom to their zeal for athletic mastery, the publication stays committed to being the voice of Blue Eagle excellence.

As our student-athletes strive to scale daring heights, let us, the Ateneo community, rally with them in every fight, fall, and victory.

mens-basketball.title: Rising Above
mens-basketball.article:
FOLLOWING A tough UAAP Season 87 showing, the Ateneo Men’s 3x3 Basketball Team looks to turn the page after their one-win campaign.

With second-year Head Coach and former Ateneo standout Nico Salva, the Blue Eagles continue their mission of building a more competitive program for the upcoming season. This mission was reflected in last season’s squad, composed of Andre Tan, Danger Tupas, Adam Dela Cruz, and Sam Reyes.

For Season 88, Ateneo aims to showcase the lessons that they have learned and embrace the growth from last season’s challenges. Repping the court this time around will be Team A mainstays Shawn Tuano, Drew Bongo, Kyle Gamber, and Thirdy Ebdane.

As 3x3 basketball continues to rise in popularity, the Katipunan-based unit remains determined to reclaim their place at the top of the sport in the UAAP arena. With a renewed focus and sense of teamwork, the Blue Eagles are ready to soar and get buckets this Season 88.

Editor's Note: The publication has chosen to feature Head Coach Nico Salva in lieu of a team captain, with the finalization of the Men’s 3x3 Basketball roster still in progress prior to the completion of the primer.

womens-basketball.title: The gold standard
womens-basketball.article:
SHOCKING THE UAAP basketball scene with their Cinderella first-place finish in Season 87, the Ateneo Women’s 3x3 Basketball Team sets their sight on a repeat title in Season 88 to prove that their breakthrough was no fluke.

After capturing their first-ever gold medal finish in last year’s competition, Head Coach PJ Navarro, alongside confirmed returnees Kai Oani and Lauren Lopez, are back in tow in pursuit of a back-to-back championship.

The Blue and White enters the season eager to deliver another impressive showing under Head Coach Navarro. As defending champions, the Blue Eagles embrace both the challenge of heightened expectations and the pressures that come with it.

Following their narrow exit in the semifinals on the 5-on-5 stage, Ateneo’s perennial 3x3 squad is intent on reasserting their place among the UAAP’s elite.

That focus now shifts to the 3x3 circuit, where belief forged in gold and resolve strengthened by adversity fuel the Katipunan-based squad’s bid to remain the gold standard of the Women’s division.

Editor's Note: The publication has chosen to feature Head Coach PJ Navarro in lieu of a team captain, with the finalization of the Women’s 3x3 Basketball roster still in progress prior to the completion of the primer.

mens-blitz-chess.title: Setting the tempo
mens-blitz-chess.article:
With the introduction of the Blitz and Rapid Chess Tournaments in Season 87, the Ateneo Men’s Chess Team (AMCT) capped their maiden Blitz campaign in last place after struggling to find dominant form on the boards.

Despite their struggles, the Blue and White successfully secured individual honors for their exploits, headlined by silver medalist Manuel Maglunog and bronze medalist Knarf Batislaong.

Running it back with the same flock of Blue Eagles from last semester’s Classical Tournament, Classical medalists Team Captain Khalil Kis-ing and promising rookie Ritchie James Abeleda aim to translate their first semester success in the faster-paced format. As veterans like Batislaong and Maglunog return to the board, the team not only has an obvious pedigree, but also the chances of team glory.

With a mixture of returning individual prowess and newfound team chemistry, Ateneo sets out to go as far as possible in their journey up the chess pedestal.

womens-blitz-chess.title: Built to blitz
womens-blitz-chess.article:
LIKE LIGHTNING—the Ateneo Women’s Blitz Chess Team returns to the UAAP with an instant attack.

Coming off a stunning championship clinch, the Blue Eagles are eager to keep steady, finding strength in their tempo. Crowned and cunning, this Jan Garcia-coached unit intends to carry a mindset of focus, grit, and learning as they look to dominate the boards.

This season, the Blue and White is coming in with its cast of seasoned gunners.. Among the returning seniors are Kristine Flores, Jiessel Marino, and Glesit Tatoy, together with juniors Alphecca Gonzales and Team Captain Elayza Villa. With a legacy to leave, these veterans are dedicated to solidifying a lasting lineage by priming emerging rookies, including Francine Magpily to take the mantle.

For the team, this sport became a two-way learning process that reminds them to always keep their feet on the ground. According to the team, they are transformed by the game as much as they change it in every move they make. With much space to flourish, the regal Women’s Blitz Chess powerhouse awaits their turn to make their tactical strike.

mens-volleyball.title: Swinging for the fences
mens-volleyball.article:
EAGER TO bounce back from last season’s fifth-place finish, the Ateneo Men’s Volleyball Team returns with renewed fire to secure a Final Four berth this year. The Blue Eagles seek redemption as they turn experience from hard-earned lessons into wins on the taraflex.

With a strengthened core, the Katipunan-based squad has sturdy shoulders to rely on. Team Captain Jian Salarzon, along with Lance De Castro, Amil Pacinio, and returning Outside Hitter Aimar Okeke headline the roster as they take their final dance for the Blue and White.

Another shot at the UAAP volleyball crown is well within reach for the senior-laden team, as they remain boosted by the ardent rhythm of Season 87’s Most Valuable Player Kennedy Batas.

Adding dimensions to the lineup, UAAP Boys’ Volleyball standout and Outside Hitter Pao Medino debuts to bring high-caliber offense for the Blue and White, accompanying his fellow young guns Opposite Spiker Preece Atendido and Setter Eijra Taluban who both showed promising performances at the 2025 V-League Collegiate Challenge.

With a chance to break through, Ateneo is ready to elevate and detonate in Season 88.

womens-volleyball.title: Turning the tides
womens-volleyball.article:
AFTER THREE consecutive seasons of falling short of the Final Four, the Ateneo Women’s Volleyball Team returns with renewed resolve to reassert themselves among the league’s elite.

Though injuries defined much of their previous campaign, the Blue Eagles showed grit in pushing through adversity, while remaining a competitive force in the collegiate volleyball scene.

At the helm of Ateneo’s campaign is veteran setter Taks Fujimoto, entrusted with steering the Blue and White’s on-court gameplay. Alongside her are JLo Delos Santos and Zel Tsunashima, who enter the year eager to showcase their renewed strength and impact after recovering from major injuries.

On the youth front, sophomores Alex Montoro and Jihan Chuatico enter the season intent on building their legacy as two of the league’s promising young talents.

Built around a blend of proven veterans and rising talents, the AWVT enters Season 88 with renewed confidence and a clearer sense of direction toward sustained success.

mens-fencing.title: Lunging to greatness
mens-fencing.article:
WITH THE depleted squad last UAAP Season 87, the Ateneo Men’s Fencing Team (AMFeT) left the piste tattered and bruised, finishing last. Newly appointed team captain, Andre Agatep, strives to continue his stellar form last season as the Blue Eagles strike for greater heights with a rejuvenated roster.

Stepping into the shoes of former captain Mico Suplico, Agatep aims to continue his exploits on the piste, building on a podium finish last season. Alongside him, incoming rookie Adam Aceron aims to resume his colorful high school career in Loyola Heights, representing the Blue and White in the sabre discipline.

Bringing much-needed experience to the table, Toby Cabrera and Alfonso Biason will attempt to capture a top-three finish for the Kaptiunan-based team this season.

With Aceron and Agatep’s youthful flair paired with Biason and Cabrera’s experience, the AMFeT will be pointing their sabres to capture a podium finish. Redemption is firmly in sight for the fencers from Loyola Heights.

womens-fencing.title: Sharper than ever
womens-fencing.article:
FLYING INTO UAAP Season 88, the Ateneo Women’s Fencing Team (AWFeT) enters with renewed determination to build on last season’s success.

Accomplished épée fencer and Team Captain Francesca Bernabe leads the squad with strategic insight and leadership, in hopes of carrying over her experiences from previous seasons.

Further empowering the team is decorated national athlete Kaikaku Dela Serna, who recently represented the Philippines as part of the women’s sabre team at the Southeast Asian Games.

Veteran épée fencer Yelena Sofia Martinez and sabre user Patricia Cablay also look to anchor the team with their solid experience. Meanwhile, sabre fencers Maiev Boy and Danica Castro, épée fencer AJ Palo and foil fencer Hannah Moricen round out the team’s depth.

In the advent of another season, the AWFeT is as eager as ever to set foot on the piste and turn their hard work into decisive victories. With a balanced mix of seasoned leadership and new talent, the Blue Eagles will give their all in every bout and once more reach for fencing glory.

womens-tennis.title: Back in business
womens-tennis.article:
AFTER A challenging UAAP Season 87 campaign, the Ateneo Women’s Tennis Team enters the fold with a renewed hunger for success and a redefined focus.

New faces Indi Fandino, Eloh Castolo, and highly touted recruit Casey Padilla join the squad, ready to give the Blue and White a much-needed boost. With the return of Ateneo ace Althea Ong and Co-captains Althea Martirez and Chelsea Roque, the trio is ready to guide the young Blue Eagles and reinforce the Katipunan-based squad for another season.

As the Blue Eagles enter a new season, the lessons from last year take center stage as they focus on building consistency and elevating their play.

Although the team is challenged to find team chemistry on the court anew, the Blue Eagles’ flight path is clear: to compete, grow, and reestablish themselves as contenders in the UAAP.

mens-tennis.title: Back in contention
mens-tennis.article:
SHAKING OFF a bruising 3-9 record that stung through Season 87, the Ateneo Men’s Tennis Team (AMTT) is locked in on punching a ticket to the Final Four.

Last season, the Blue Eagles finished five games behind the Final Four cutoff as defending champions University of Santo Tomas Male Tennisters swept them twice in 5-0 shutouts en route to their third consecutive title.

Ateneo also faced additional roster gaps in its push back into contention following the departure of veteran Stef Gurria and Gian Camingue.

Since then, the Blue Eagles have built around Season 87 standouts and current co-captains JB Cuarto and JD Velez, with freshmen Vito Singson and Juan Pabillore entering the Eagle’s nest.

Singson, a sought-after recruit in junior tennis, joins forces with Pabillore, who is fresh off his 2025 Palarong Pambansa stint. The seven-month grind prepared the rookies for Coach Ricardo Lagac Jr.’s system before Season 88’s opening serve.

While the rookies settled in, the Katipunan-based team mined last season’s challenges to seek new strategies, focusing on more drills for high-pressure moments. Now, the AMTT heads into Season 88 ready to climb back into Final Four contention.

mens-taekwondo.title: Push to podium
mens-taekwondo.article:
LOOKING TO push their way to the podium, the Ateneo Men’s Taekwondo Team kicks off UAAP Season 88 with a fresh lineup.

Last Season 87, the Blue Eagles came up short in the Men’s Kyorugi division with a last-place finish. While the Poomsae teams headed to the finals in three of five categories, they still came away empty-handed, with Joaquin Tuzon placing fourth in Individual Male Poomsae.

Looking to shift the tides this season, the Katipunan-based squad has tapped four recruits. In particular, Michael Cabaluna Jr., Kier Cuyugan, and Randz Gaupo joined the Men’s Kyorugi team, while Jerome Castro entered the Poomsae squad.

The new roster has already shown promise in the preseason, collecting medals at the 2025 Philippine Taekwondo Association Taekwondo Championships and bronze at the 2025 Smart MVP Sports Foundation National Interschool Taekwondo Championships.

With its lineup set on the mats and captains Angelo Santiago and Tuzon ready to make their mark, Ateneo is determined to seize the chance to return to the map and bring home hardware.

womens-taekwondo.title: Reaching greater heights
womens-taekwondo.article:
AIMING HIGH for Season 88, the Ateneo Women’s Taekwondo Team (AWTT) is undaunted in their mission to step on the podium.

Leading the Kyorugi team are Rigel Dumat-ol and Kamille Calaycay. The roster features returning veterans Kenshin Bonos and Keir Atendido, alongside rookie Stefanie Leones.

After climbing from sixth place in Season 86, to fourth in Season 87, the team is determined to build even more momentum this year.

Carrying the same hunger, the Poomsae team is set on pushing past their sixth-place finish in Season 86 and their fourth-place finish from Season 87. Bolstered by a mix of veterans and rookies, the Poomsae team welcomes rookie Elizabeth Borres, who has bagged two bronze medals at the Asian Taekwondo Federation Championships.

Graduating Team Captain Elaine Borres and Co-captain Mariea Komicho lead the team with their eyes set on a return to the top three. With confidence from their pre-season medals in the National Best of the Best Taekwondo Championships and National Interschool Championships, the Poomsae team continues to grow under Coaches Roel Borja Jr. and Vincent Rodriguez.

As a whole, the AWTT steps into the season ready to showcase their growth and potential for a podium finish.

mens-judo.title: Tatami Takeover
mens-judo.article:
CARRYING A renewed sense of grit and confidence from a stellar offseason, the Ateneo Men’s Judo Team enters Season 88 with hunger, purpose, and unfinished business.

Team Captain Trev Apostol leads an Ateneo lineup riding the momentum of a statement offseason. This period of preparation was highlighted by a strong medal haul at the National Capital Region Judo Association Tournament, bannered by Pete Fabre earning gold, Keoni Dylim winning silver, and Eric Rodriguez and Apostol receiving podium finishes.

Adding more firepower to the squad are Philippine Ultimate Judo Championships bronze medalist Josh Bolipata, Aldwyn Thor, and David Tan. Meanwhile, the heavier weights will be bannered by Ethan Sarte at -90kg, Quino Ampeloquio and Jiro Barrientos at -100kg, and Lim Realda anchoring +100kg.

With the team’s consistent fourth placing in the last two seasons, the question now stands: does the Blue and White’s six-season podium drought end here?

One thing is certain—this squad is relentless and hungry, determined to shake up the collegiate judo landscape this year.

womens-judo.title: Fight for redemption
womens-judo.article:
EYES SET on reclaiming the podium, the Ateneo Women’s Judo Team (AWJT) enters the new season with determination in every grapple and throw.

The Blue Eagles are geared up for success, with a roster consisting of returning veterans and promising rookies. Notably, the roster also features veteran and Southeast Asian Games gold medalist Maxine Mababangloob, alongside high school standouts Elyssa Cao and Khristine Anonuevo. Leading the squad this year are captains Robynne Gonzales and Janelle Panes, who are set on ensuring that each member of the team continues to aim for the best.

Shaking off the previous year’s woes, the Blue and White’s pre-season run served as a testament to their growth, with Gonzales and Panes bagging two bronze medals in the Philippine Ultimate Judo Championships. Panes also secured gold in the NCR Judo Association Tournament alongside Cao, Rica Escalada, and Bella De Leon, who each earned bronze medals.

With the guidance of program head Ali Sulit and coaches Robert Divina, Gilbert Ramirez, and Alvin Mendoza, the team carries the lessons of last season, setting their sights on redemption.

mlbb.title: Usurping Battlefields
mlbb.article:
FUELED BY resilience, the Ateneo Blue Eagles strive to rise from the ashes in the UAAP Season 88 Mobile Legends: Bang Bang tournament. Washing off last season’s setbacks, Team Captains Angelo Olvida and Aaron Yuk Hong Sze hold the reins in steering the squad with purpose and undeterred composure.

After falling short of a win last season, the rebuilding unit retraced their steps in search for their harmony on the battlefield. Investing heavily in recalibrating in-game communication, the Blue Eagles committed to utilizing more disciplined win conditions.

Supporting the foundation are middle laner Zosi Nera Jr. and gold laner Sebastian Antolin, alongside new blood jungler Mathew Reunir, who adds firepower to Ateneo’s growing lineup.

With their team chemistry steadily taking shape, the Blue and White enters the season grounded—carrying confidence anchored in refined rotations. To further fortify their preparation, the domination mindset is instilled as they surge in the tournament, taking down towers one by one to secure victories en route to the top.

valorant.title: Aiming higher
valorant.article:
ENTERING THE new UAAP Season, the Ateneo Valorant Team is locked in on building beyond last season’s success, carrying over its momentum from a hard-fought run. With the first year of UAAP Esports behind them, the Blue Eagles head into Season 88 with a promising and determined roster.

Team Captain Juancho Garcia sets the pace for the Blue and White, armed with strategic approaches to take on this season’s high-pressure matches. Anchoring the team’s foundation are Joaquin Antonio and Alonso Lopez, both seasoned veterans whose experience steadies the team under pressure.

Rounding the roster are Jack Santiago, Michael Ablang, and Hans Yu, each adding flexibility across roles and the team’s overall adaptability. During the offseason, the Ateneo Valorant Team focused on refining team coordination and tightening game meta execution.

With renewed focus and sharpened aims, the Ateneo Valorant Team enters Season 88 intent on proving that last season’s bronze finish was only the beginning. No longer content with simply reaching the podium, the Blue Eagles look forward to chasing a championship run this season.

nba2k.title: They got next
nba2k.article:
CHAMPIONSHIPS HAVE  become the standard for the Ateneo NBA 2K Team following a historic repeat in UAAP Season 87. That standard faces an early test as the league introduces a shift from the 1v1 Play Now mode to the more demanding 5v5 Pro-Am format.

With no returning players from last season’s championship roster, the Blue and White begin their title defense with a clean slate. Head Coach Nite Alparas, also at the helm of eGilas Pilipinas, leads this new chapter and is tasked with molding a team built for five-on-five competition.

As the final lineup takes shape, the current player pool composed of Jake Madamba, Banjo Dungca, Andrei Co, Miguel Zamudio, Ram Santiago, and Basty Umali competes for roles in a system that values chemistry and execution.

For the Blue Eagles, chasing a third-straight title will hinge on adaptability, discipline, and trust in the system—principles that have long defined the Blue and White and kept the crown firmly in their hands.

streetdance.title: Taking center stage
streetdance.article:
THE FLOOR is set, the lights are bright, and the stage is ready as the Company of Ateneo Dancers (CADs) returns to take the spotlight once more.

Last season, the team performed a Michael Jackson-inspired routine that showcased intricate choreography and energy, finishing in fifth place overall. This momentum carried into the offseason, as CADs made waves in the competitive circuit, including a strong showing at the Dance Supremacy Kings and Queens and the World of Dance Summit 2026.

This year, the roster blends experienced dancers with rising talents, promising energy, tight formations, and dynamic performances. With Jan Imbao and Celina Baltazar as co-captains, the Blue Eagles are aiming for a podium finish by elevating their craft and grooving their way into one of UAAP’s most awaited competitions.

Momentum now meets opportunity as CADs take on another run in the UAAP Season 88 Streetdance competition.

womens-softball.title: A new flight begins
womens-softball.article:
THE BLUE Eagles soar into the UAAP Season 88 Women’s Softball with fierce spirit and bright promise. After battling through adversity in Season 87, this year’s team blends seasoned leadership with emerging rookies, marking a transitional chapter for the Blue and White.

At the forefront of the campaign is graduating Captain Ashya Tuprio, whose leadership provides a steady anchor for the Blue Eagles. Alongside her are Co-Captain Andeng Daquigan and fellow senior Riz Bulatao, whose experiences will help set the tone for a developing squad.

The team’s veteran core guides a youthful roster through the UAAP scene, while setting standards that will last beyond the season. Notable additions to the unit include Zyrah De Guzman, Katrice Ditchon, Minelli Profeta, Marvs Romano, and Ateneo Women’s Football Team mainstays Angely Alferez, Tootchie Eval, and Alyssa Gonzalez.

Under Head Coach Joan Locsin, this young but united squad is not only rebuilt—they are reborn. Season 88 promises Blue Eagle discipline and resolve as Ateneo chases brighter days on the diamond.

baseball.title: Pressure makes diamonds
baseball.article:
SWINGING THEIR way back onto the diamond, the Ateneo Baseball Team (ABT) enters Season 88 amid a transitioning period. Despite retooling over the summer, this hungry squad maintains the competitive fuel of the Blue and White.

Team Captains Angelo “Bop” Bernardo and Joshua De Juras lead the way for the ABT, filling in the holes left by predecessors Alejandro Mendoza and Zeke Laygo.

Returning to the base are veteran hitters Dax Fabella, Matthew San Juan, and Alfy Tueres—who all aim to bring slugging expertise on the field. The ABT also exhibits a dangerous rotation this season, flanked by pitcher Lucas Atendido, who had an impressive Season 87 on the mound.

On the forefront of Ateneo’s reinforcements are nine new rookies, headlined by Ryu Garcia, Jayden Ponce, and Mikaelo Osorio. This new batch of athletes aims to add athleticism and agility to an experienced and battle-tested bullpen.

Heading into Season 88 with new talent and undeniable hustle, the ABT are ready to face the top teams in their league, possessing the potential to shake up the UAAP baseball scene.
